title: Multi-Raft Partitioned Transaction Ledger
subtitle: Linearizable Consensus, Log Compaction and Leader Leases under WAN Partitions
problem_statement: A distributed financial ledger shards transaction ranges into 128 independent Raft consensus groups. During cross-datacenter WAN link flapping, heartbeats are delayed, causing frequent leader elections, split-vote thundering herds, and tail latency spikes exceeding 1,200ms.

faded_bug.description: Missing randomized election timeout and pre-vote phase causes repeated split votes during network partitions.

invariants.description: Quorum acknowledgement (majority = 2/3) must precede all read/write commits.

probing_ladder.stage_1_validation: Explain the difference between standard Raft read through state machine log commit vs ReadIndex / LeaseRead optimization.
probing_ladder.stage_2_tightening: If leader election takes 300ms, how do you handle incoming client transactions during the gap? Does your gateway buffer or return 503?
probing_ladder.stage_3_adversarial: A partitioned leader continues serving reads because its local lease has not expired, but physical clock drifted forward. Can stale reads occur?
probing_ladder.stage_4_squeeze: Cross-datacenter bandwidth costs $0.02 per GB. How do you compress and batch append entries without violating the 35ms P99 SLA?

counter_probes.counter_question: If you replicate every single analytical query through the Raft log, what happens to disk I/O and Raft log compaction frequency?
counter_probes.expected_staff_answer: Read queries must NOT be appended to the log. ReadIndex or time-bounded leader leases (validated with monotonic clocks) provide linearizable reads with zero write amplification.
